document_notes: Page 289 contains the continuation of the entry for T. Avidius Quietus (PIR² A 1410), who is attested as legatus Aug. pr. pr. of Britannia.

entries.relevance_notes: Explicitly named as 'Legatus Aug. pr. pr. Britanniae a. 98 (vel 99)'.

segments.identification_and_sources: Plin. ep. 9, 13, 15; 6, 29, 1. Plutarchus de frat. amore, quaest. conv. 2, 1, 5. Macrob. 7, 3, 15. IG 5, 1. CIL XI 660.
segments.offices_and_career: legatus legionis VIII Augustae, proconsul Achaiae sub Domitiano, legatus Aug. pr. pr. Britanniae a. 98 (vel 99).
segments.governorship_attestation: Legatus Aug. pr. pr. Britanniae a. 98 (vel 99) t. 6, si recte ut videtur editores in dipl. mil. cognomen Quieti suppleverunt.
segments.family_and_social_relations: Frater Avidii Nigrini. Amicus Plutarchi, Plinii, Sosii Senecionis. Familiaris Thraseae Paeti, Aufidii Modesti, Arriae et Fanniae. Pater Avidii Quieti (proconsul Asiae sub Hadriano).
segments.prosopographical_commentary: Discussion of his proconsulship of Achaia, his consulship (possibly in 97), and his properties in Rome (Esquiliae, Quirinalis) and Sardinia.

notes: Friend of Pliny the Younger and Plutarch.

governorship_factoids.exact_text: Legatus Aug. pr. pr. Britanniae a. 98 (vel 99)
notes: The cognomen Quietus is restored by editors in the military diploma.
Earlier scholars incorrectly thought he governed Thrace under Domitian.
Dated to around 95 AD by Pomtow.

entry_notes: The entry discusses his career, family, and social circle, including his friendship with Plutarch and Pliny.
